name: GitHub, Inc.
subcategory: code hosting / developer platform / AI coding (Copilot)
origin_detail: Founded 2008 in San Francisco by Chris Wanstrath, PJ Hyett and Tom Preston-Werner (with Scott Chacon); ran without outside funding and profitably until a 2012 Series A
openness_notes: The platform itself (GitHub.com, GitHub Enterprise Server, Copilot service) is proprietary; GitHub's openness is as host and steward of other people's open source. It has open-sourced peripheral tools (Electron, Atom, libgit2, Linguist, gh CLI, Desktop). Rated 1 (only peripheral clients/tools open) throughout.

license_history.license: Proprietary SaaS; free hosting for public open-source repos
license_history.note: Paid private repos funded the company

exit_events.note: Closed 25 Oct 2018 as a $7.5B stock transaction (incl. $1.3B cash for vested equity awards and escrow); goodwill $5.44B; Nat Friedman became CEO

risk_events: Jun 2018: Microsoft acquisition news triggered lock-in fears; GitLab reported >100,000 repositories imported within days (#movingtogitlab), though GitHub's user growth continued
Jun 2022: GitHub announced the sunset of its open-source Atom editor (archived 15 Dec 2022) to focus on Microsoft's VS Code and Codespaces
Aug 2025: CEO Thomas Dohmke announced departure (left end-2025); Microsoft did not replace the CEO role and folded GitHub into its CoreAI division, ending largely independent operation
robustness: Network-effect monopoly for open-source hosting (180M+ developers and 630M projects per Octoverse 2025) backed by Microsoft; revenue run rate $2B in mid-2024 with Copilot driving >40% of growth. As a closed, single-vendor platform it is a structural dependency for the open-source ecosystem: the code is portable (git) but issues, CI, social graph and package registries are not.
physical_science_relevance: The default host for scientific code, data-analysis notebooks and open-hardware designs; Zenodo-GitHub integration makes it a de facto archive pipeline for citable research software.
openness_effect_assessment: GitHub captured value from openness without being open itself: free hosting for public repos created the network effects that made paid private/enterprise hosting and later Copilot (trained largely on public code) valuable. The $7.5B exit and $2B run rate came from intermediating open-source collaboration, while its closed platform has drawn lock-in criticism rather than forks.
key_takeaway: GitHub is the clearest case of a closed platform built on top of the open-source commons: openness in the ecosystem, not in the product, generated its value, and AI (Copilot) became its growth engine after acquisition. Its 2025 absorption into Microsoft CoreAI shows the commons' central infrastructure is now controlled by a big-tech AI strategy.
